definition: To quickly sort incoming problems by how urgent they are.
business_context_example: Morning triage takes twenty minutes and saves the rest of the day.

definition: The list of reported problems waiting to be handled.
business_context_example: The queue was 60 tickets on Monday and 12 by Wednesday.

definition: To give a reported problem to a specific person.
business_context_example: Assign it to whoever fixed the same thing last month.
translation_bg: да възложа заявка на конкретен човек

definition: How urgent a problem is compared with the others.
business_context_example: Everything arrives marked high priority. Almost nothing is.

definition: How much damage a problem is causing.
business_context_example: One person can't print. That's low severity, whatever they tell you.

definition: A written promise about how fast problems will be answered and fixed.
business_context_example: The agreement gives us four hours to respond, not four hours to fix.

definition: To pass a problem to a more specialised support team.
business_context_example: If it isn't solved in thirty minutes, escalate to second line.
translation_bg: да прехвърля към по-висока линия поддръжка

definition: To make a closed problem active again because it came back.
business_context_example: He reopened the ticket four days later with the same error.

definition: What the user sees when something is wrong.
business_context_example: The symptom is a blank screen. The cause is somewhere else entirely.

definition: Happening sometimes, not every time.
business_context_example: Intermittent faults are the hardest, because they behave while you watch.
translation_bg: появяващ се от време на време

definition: To make the same problem happen on your own machine.
business_context_example: I couldn't replicate the issue until I tried it on an old phone.
translation_bg: да възпроизведа проблема при себе си

definition: To reduce the number of possible causes.
business_context_example: Two questions narrowed it down from everything to the Wi-Fi.

definition: The exact actions that make the problem appear.
business_context_example: A ticket without steps to reproduce is a ticket nobody can start.

definition: A short number or text that identifies a specific fault.
business_context_example: Read me the error code exactly, including the letters.

definition: The people the problem is happening to.
business_context_example: Three affected users, all in the Varna office, all on the same floor.

definition: To find which single part is creating the problem.
business_context_example: We isolated the cause by unplugging things one at a time.

definition: To guide a person through a task one step at a time.
business_context_example: I walked her through it on the phone while she described the screen.
translation_bg: да преведа някого стъпка по стъпка

definition: One small instruction at a time.
business_context_example: Step by step, and wait for them to say 'done' before the next one.

definition: A connection that lets support see or control a user's screen.
business_context_example: A two-minute remote session beats twenty minutes of describing.
translation_bg: отдалечена сесия, свързване към чужд компютър

definition: Showing your screen to someone else during a call.
business_context_example: Can you screen share? I'd rather see it than imagine it.

definition: To switch a device fully off, wait, and switch it on again.
business_context_example: Power cycle the router: off, thirty seconds, on.
translation_bg: пълно изключване и включване на устройство

definition: To leave a system and enter it again.
business_context_example: Log out and back in. It solves more than anyone wants to admit.
translation_bg: да изляза и да вляза отново

definition: To remove a program and install it again.
business_context_example: Reinstall it only after the simpler things have failed.

definition: Small software that lets a computer use a device.
business_context_example: The printer worked again once the driver was updated.

definition: Giving a user a new password so they can get in again.
business_context_example: Monday morning is half password resets, every single week.

definition: Said without technical words.
business_context_example: In plain English: the file is too big to send.

definition: Specialist words that outsiders don't understand.
business_context_example: Every word of that sentence was jargon, and she was too polite to say so.

definition: To say the same thing in different words.
business_context_example: If they go quiet, rephrase it. Don't repeat it louder.

definition: To explain something complicated in smaller parts.
business_context_example: Break it down into three steps and they'll follow all three.

definition: The person who actually uses the system day to day.
business_context_example: The end user doesn't care whose fault it is.

definition: Without technical knowledge or training.
business_context_example: Write the note for a non-technical reader and everyone benefits.

definition: To make sure the other person has followed you.
business_context_example: Check understanding by asking what they see now, not 'is that clear?'

definition: Please wait patiently for a moment.
business_context_example: Bear with me, I'm opening your account now.

definition: To not hang up during a phone call.
business_context_example: Stay on the line while it restarts, it takes about a minute.

definition: To investigate a problem.
business_context_example: I'll look into it and call you back before twelve.

definition: To say sorry for the trouble something has caused.
business_context_example: Apologise once, properly, then talk about the fix.

definition: To contact someone again to get an answer.
business_context_example: Chase up the supplier. They've had our question since Tuesday.

definition: A short message saying where things stand.
business_context_example: A progress update every hour keeps the phone quiet.

definition: To send something as a written record.
business_context_example: Put it in writing so the next person on shift knows too.
translation_bg: да го напиша, да остане писмено

definition: Something that works for now while a real solution is prepared.
business_context_example: The temporary fix is still running three months later. They always are.

definition: A solution that removes the problem for good.
business_context_example: The permanent fix needs the supplier, so it waits until Monday.

definition: Testing showed nothing wrong with the device.
business_context_example: It came back marked 'no fault found', which helps nobody.

definition: A problem caused by how the person used the system.
business_context_example: Write 'user error' in your head, never in the ticket.

definition: A problem that keeps coming back.
business_context_example: Four tickets in a month makes it a recurring issue, not bad luck.

definition: To record that a problem has been solved.
business_context_example: Don't mark it as resolved until the user says it works.

definition: To write down what was done so others can repeat it.
business_context_example: Document the fix while you still remember the third step.

definition: A comment on a ticket that the customer never sees.
business_context_example: The internal note said 'third time this week'.

definition: To give a task to another person or team.
business_context_example: Pass it on to the network team with everything you've already tried.
translation_bg: да предам на друг човек или екип

definition: A record of who did what, and when.
business_context_example: The audit trail showed the setting changed at 02:14, by nobody.

definition: A short written account of what happened.
business_context_example: One page. Her write-up saved the next person two hours.
